The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Davis Building Rehabilitation
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This is NOT a solicitation. This is not a Request for Bid, Proposal, or Quote. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment to the Government. NO SOLICITATION OR ATTACHMENTS are available for this notice. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this survey. Any information submitted by respondents to this Sources Sought notice is strictly voluntary. Responses will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future Request for Quote (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB) or Request for Proposal (RFP), if any are issued. This survey is for market research purposes only. Only contractors capable of performing this type of work should respond to this notice. INTRODUCTION The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Detroit District, is issuing this Sources Sought notice and conducting market research as a means to identify interest and capabilities of both small and large business entities to provide design and construction services for the Davis Building Rehabilitation project located at the Soo Locks Complex in Sault Sainte Marie, Michigan. The information collected will be used to help determine the appropriate strategy to solicit and award the project. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. All small business set-aside socioeconomic categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. REQUIREMENT* for the Davis Building Rehabilitation project Summary Scope: The contractor will provide all materials, labor, equipment, supervision, and administration as necessary for repairs, rehabilitation, and construction to the historic Davis Pump Well Building located at the Soo Locks in Sault Sainte Marie, MI. The historic building was built in the early 1900s and is located on the island between the Poe Lock and the Davis Lock (now the New Lock currently in construction). Referenced picture of the Davis Building attached to this notice. Primary purpose of the building was to facilitate the dewatering of the locks for regular operations, but pumps are now decommissioned and removed due to construction of the New Lock. The facility is intended to be repurposed to facilitate up to 50 maintenance personnel including, but not limited to, locker rooms, break rooms, kitchen/laundry and staff offices. The Davis Building currently provides approximately 4,200 square-feet of ground floor office space with approximately 4,200 square-foot of basement that houses mechanical and electrical systems. Due to project location, barge-based transportation and load handling equipment will be required. The schedule is estimated to take 36 months, which includes up to 12 months for design and 24 months for construction. Project will include but is not limited to the following: Repair or replace deteriorating clips holding the limestone fascia to the building. Design and implement a water mitigation plan to manage stormwater runoff from roof downspouts and prevent moisture intrusion in the basement. Replace all windows and doors. Design and construct a new subterranean locker room in place of the existing pump well access ramp that is no longer needed and complete all necessary earthwork, backfill, structural compaction, and surface grading to eliminate the ramp opening and restore surface elevations flush with surrounding grade. Construct a mezzanine level above the first-floor office space (within the first-floor footprint) to accommodate additional locker room space. Reconfigure existing restrooms to maximize utilization. Upgrade all mechanical, electrical, and IT systems to accommodate building occupancy, usage, and security. Install fire alarms and suppression system. NOTE: Lead and asbestos abatement is anticipated as part of this project. *Please note the description of the requirement is subject to change. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is anticipated to be 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, which has a small business size standard of $45M in average annual receipts. Place of Performance: Sault Ste. Marie, Chippewa County, MI Both Large and Small Business firms who are interested are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought Notice. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. Anticipated Solicitation: Winter 2026 Anticipated Period of Performance: 36 Months SOURCES SOUGHT RESPONSES If your organization has the potential capacity and capability to perform this type of work, please complete the attached questionnaire and submit via email to Contract Specialist, Joseph Orlando at joseph.orlando@usace.army.mil and Contracting Officer, Lisa May at lisa.m.may@usace.army.mil no later than November 12, 2026 at 2:00 PM (Eastern). Please reference in the subject line "SOURCES SOUGHT Davis Building Rehabilitation� All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought notice. RESPONDENTS WILL NOT BE CONTACTED REGARDING THEIR SUBMISSION OR INFORMATION GATHERED AS A RESULT OF THE SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE.

title: Pre-Solicitation: Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within Springfield, Illinois. Home Confinement radius within 200 miles of the RRC Faciliy.
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC27R00000013 Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services with a facility located within Illinois Counties of Adams, Brown, Pike, Scott, Morgan, Cass, Menard, Sangamon, Macoupin, Greene, Montgomery, Christian, Dewitt, Macon, Piatt, Champaign, Moultrie, Coles, Douglas, Ford, Vermillion, and Edgar. Home Confinement radius is within 200 of the RRC facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Illinois Counties of Adams, Brown, Pike, Scott, Morgan, Cass, Menard, Sangamon, Macoupin, Greene, Montgomery, Christian, Dewitt, Macon, Piatt, Champaign, Moultrie, Coles, Douglas, Ford, Vermillion, and Edgar. Home Confinement radius is within 200 of the RRC facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC in-house requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 26 beds (22 males and 4 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum of 50 beds (43 males and 7 females). The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 13 placements for the base year and an estimated maximum of 25 placements. The anticipated solicitation will include separate pricing for RRC in-house services and Home Confinement services using a tiered pricing structure based on average daily population (ADP). Monthly pricing will apply when the ADP is 20 or fewer for RRC services and 10 or fewer for Home Confinement services. Daily pricing tiers will apply to RRC populations of 21 to 30, 31 to 40, and 41 or more, and Home Confinement populations of 11 to 15, 16 to 20, and 21 or more. The solicitation will establish the final pricing schedule and requirements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and Home Confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. Offerors will be required to provide separate prices for each service. The Government reserves the right to make an award deemed to be in the best interest of the Government, consistent with the terms of the solicitation. RFP 15BRRC27R00000013 is anticipated to be available on or about November 17, 2026, following a minimum 15-calendar-day presolicitation notice period on SAM.gov. The Government anticipates allowing at least 30 calendar days following solicitation issuance for submission of proposals. The exact proposal due date and time will be specified in the solicitation. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. Downloading instructions are provided on the website. Future information concerning this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed through SAM.gov. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring the website to ensure they have the most current information concerning this acquisition. This is a presolicitation notice only and is not a request for proposals. Proposals are not being requested at this time. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the forthcoming solicitation, which will be considered by the agency. No collect calls will be accepted. Telephone or written requests for hard copies of the solicitation will not be accepted. Update: Sources Sought Questions and Answers The Federal Bureau of Prisons has added the attached �Springfield, IL RFI Questions and Answers� document to provide responses to questions received regarding Sources Sought/RFI 15BRRC27R for Residential Reentry Center (RRC) and Home Confinement (HC) services in the Springfield, Illinois area. The sources-sought response period closed on October 28, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time. This update does not reopen or extend that response period. title: P-271, E-130J Main Operating and Training Base, MCAS Cherry Point, NC
description: This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to make notice of a proposed contract action for performing pre-construction services and construction services for P-271, E-130J Main Operating & Training Base, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project constructs all operational and support facilities for E-130J Main Operating Base (MOB) and Fleet Replacement Squadron (FRS) training campus at the Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) in Cherry Point, NC. New construction facilities include an aircraft parking apron, aircraft access apron, taxiway, three-bay aircraft maintenance hangar, training building, Mobile Support Unit operational compound, and an aircraft maintenance and ground support equipment warehouse. Renovation of existing facilities includes Building 244 for Center for Naval Aviation Technical Training (CNATT) academic and applied training functions associated with the E-130J. The Aircraft Maintenance Hangar will be a two-story building with high-bay, overhead maintenance space to support three E-130J aircraft. The hangar will be constructed as four separate buildings with expansion joints, built on deep foundations using driven precast, prestressed concrete piles. The Hangar Security Building is a single-story security guard house, outside of the PL2 security fenceline, that provides controlled access to the hangar enclave for vehicles and pedestrians. The Training Building is a predominantly single-story building, divided into four massing areas with varying roof heights. Much of the facility is low-rise, with roof heights of 16-20 feet. The Mobile Support Unit Operational Compound is a low-rise, pre-engineered long-span metal building. The Aircraft Maintenance and Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Warehouse is a low-rise, pre-engineered metal building with structural columns located along the middle of each space. The project will renovate and alter portions of Building 244 which has a total floor area of 4,356 m2 and currently supports existing CNATT functions. The project also includes significant road widening along Roosevelt Avenue and Access Roads, utility upgrades including the replacement of an electric substation, water, sewer and communications lines and a pump station. The completion time for this project is approximately 700 calendar days after award for pre-constructions services and 1,825 calendar days for construction services. P-271 is a design-bid-build project. This procurement will utilize the Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) approach and be procured in two segments: Segment I � Early Contractor Involvement Preconstruction Services and Segment II � Construction Services. Segment I � This solicitation is being advertised as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition and require both non-price (technical and past performance) and price proposals for the preconstruction efforts and utilizes the best value continuum process at FAR 15.103-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0048), Tradeoff. The basis for evaluation and evaluation factors for award will be included in the solicitation for Segment I and will those evaluation factors will carry over to Segment II. The Government intends to award three (3) contracts to three (3) contractors for the Segment I � ECI preconstruction services. Segment II � Only contractors from Segment I will be prequalified to propose on the construction services. The Segment II source selection procurement requires both non-price and price proposals for the construction and will utilize the best value continuum process at FAR 15.103-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0048), Tradeoff. The basis for evaluation and evaluation factors for award included in Segment I will carry over to Segment II in addition to the remaining technical factors. Segment II will award the construction services to only one (1) of the three (3) prequalified offerors who received an award for ECI preconstruction services in Segment I. P271 will be at the 35% design stage upon award of the ECI Preconstruction Services. The selected contractors for the ECI will work collaboratively with Designer of Record (DOR) and the Government team to improve the overall project delivery. The preconstruction services will generally include: reviewing and evaluating the design documents at specified stages of development to identify potential constructability challenges and risks; providing value engineering-style recommendations and alternative ideas to improve the final product considering cost and schedule; advising on efficient construction means and methods; providing regularly updated construction cost information with substantiating documentation; identifying construction cost and schedule risks and mitigation recommendations; and identifying opportunities to increase small business subcontractor participation. The DOR will collaborate with the Construction Contractor to ensure the design does not inhibit use of efficient construction means and methods, and to develop design solutions that avoid constructability challenges and minimize cost and schedule risks. The DOR will maintain responsibility for the quality and engineering compliance for the design, and the Construction Contractor�s involvement during the design phase does not absolve the DOR of this contractual responsibility or Architect-Engineer (AE) liability. The magnitude of construction for this project is over $1,000,000,000. The appropriate North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and the Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000. This office anticipates award of a contract for these pre-construction services by January 2027 and award of the construction by September 2028. A Sources Sought Notice (N4008526R0262) was issued on 14 August 2026 on SAM and a market survey was conducted that included an assessment of relevant qualifications and capabilities of potentially qualified firms. The Government invited prospective offerors with the capabilities of performing construction services that meet or exceed the stated requirement to submit a capabilities statement. Respondents were required to submit relevant experience in performing efforts of similar size and scope/complexity within the last ten (10) years. Based on the market research conducted for this procurement and in accordance with FAR 19.104-1(b) (DPCAP CD 2026-O0037, the Contracting Officer has determined that there is not a reasonable expectation that an adequate number of Small Business firms would respond to or be qualified to perform the requirements of this solicitation. Successful award and completion of the requirements can be achieved by soliciting the contract as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic�s Office of Small Business Programs agrees with this decision and concurs with the determination to solicit as an unrestricted procurement. No drawings or specifications will be posted with the solicitation during Segment I and are not available at this time. The solicitation will be issued by NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic on or about 12 November 2026. The solicitation number will be N40085-26-R-0262. All documents will be in Adobe PDF file format and downloadable from the PIEE and Sam.gov website. The official address to the solicitation is https://piee.eb.mil and https://www.sam.gov under �contract opportunities� when it becomes available. Contractors are encouraged to register for the solicitation when downloading from the website. Only registered contractors will be notified by email when amendments to the solicitation are issued. title: USS AMERICA (LHA-6) MATERIAL HANDLING EQUIPMENT (MHE) REFURBISHMENT
description: USS AMERICA (LHA-6) Aircraft Intermediate Maintenance Department (AIMD) employs a suite of Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to move aeronautical components, engines, support equipment, and palletized material in support of intermediate-level maintenance and flight operations. These assets are essential to aviation logistics throughput, stores onload/offload, and hangar bay and flight deck material movement. Sustained operational use, shipboard environmental exposure, and deferred depot-level maintenance have degraded the material condition of twenty three (23) assets to the point that they are non-operational or unable to hold current weight-handling certification. Ship's force personnel are qualified to operate this equipment but are neither trained nor certified to perform depot-level overhaul, load testing, or weight-handling certification. Refurbishment of these assets during the upcoming Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) will restore full MHE capability, extend equipment service life, and prevent critical work stoppages in the aviation maintenance and supply chain.

Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River.

title: Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri
description: ****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

description: ****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River.

title: Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River.

description: ****Amend 0004 posted 20261002: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0003 posted 20260925: Provide updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

title: Q301 - Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Veracyte Decipher Testing Services - Cleveland OH VAMC
description: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Requirement The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 10, intends to negotiate a sole source contract under Simplified Acquisition Procedures and the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The associated NAICS code for this is 334516, Size Standard is 1,000 employees. Product Service Code (PSC) is Q301. The sole-source contract will be awarded to: VERACYTE, INC UEI: JS7GBP6LCMN6 Description of equipment requirements: The VA Northeast Ohio Healthcare System (VANEOHS) requires continued access to specialized genomic classifier testing used to assess risk of metastasis or metastatic progression in patients with localized or advanced prostate cancer. Decipher prostate testing is a powerful diagnostic and prognostic tool that assesses risk of prostate cancer progression within the next five years post detection, biopsy or surgical removal. The test utilizes a genome-wide transcriptome assay to analyze the expression of 22 genes to generate the Decipher score. Performed on existing tissue samples obtained during biopsy or surgical removal of the prostate, prior to any radiation or hormone therapy. Indicated in localized, N1, or metastatic disease. Provides the Decipher score based on genomic characteristics of the tumor, independent of clinical and pathological factors. The score, ranging between 0 and 1, reflects tumor aggressiveness. It is the Government's belief that only the proposed candidate possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement. It is the Government's intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. IAW FAR 5.207 all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that demonstrates the ability to comply with the requirement and that competition would be advantageous to the Government. The Government will not pay for information submitted. A determination not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Area of Interest: OSW Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) Modeling and Simulation
description: The Department of War (DOW) Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) supports the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW). The Director of CAPE is the principal staff assistant to the Secretary of War for Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation. In fulfilling this role, the Director of CAPE provides independent, non-advocate, and data-driven analytical evaluations directly to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War regarding defense program investments, major force structure posture, and strategic resourcing trade-offs. The Director�s principal responsibilities include: Analyze and evaluate plans, programs, and budgets in relation to U.S. defense objectives, projected threats, allied contributions, estimated costs, and resource constraints. Review, analyze, and evaluate programs, including classified programs, for executing approved policies. Provide leadership in developing and promoting improved analytical tools and methods for analyzing national security planning and the allocation of resources. Ensure that the costs of DoW programs, including classified programs, are presented accurately and completely. Assess effects of DoW spending on the U.S. economy and evaluate alternative policies to ensure that DoW programs can be implemented efficiently. Currently, CAPE�s campaign- and mission-level Modeling and Simulation (M&S) relies on heavy, time-intensive physics engines (e.g., AFSIM) that execute discrete, bespoke combat runs. While highly detailed, these simulation approaches are too slow, computationally expensive, and inflexible to support executive-level sensitivity sweeps across multi-dimensional threat environments and Department warfighting capabilities. CAPE�s current environment leverages HPC resources that provide 1.5 terabytes (TB) of usable memory and 2,000 Central Processing Unit (CPU) cores with no wall clock time restraints. On average, individual simulation execution via AFSIM requires 1 hour of real time to complete and 20 gigabytes (GB) of accessible RAM. This constraint, coupled with sharp disparities in compute architecture, hardware availability, and security accreditation across existing CAPE enclaves restrict analysts to limited, manual workflows while preventing the execution of high-throughput, compute-intensive campaign analytics. CAPE is seeking innovative solutions to establish a next-generation modeling architecture, replacing its legacy M&S infrastructure. To dramatically compress the cycle time between defense budget queries and statistically defensible warfighting insights, the target environment must integrate three interdependent functional layers: (1) A high-performance simulation execution layer to execute large numbers of model (e.g., AFSIM) runs to span the parameter space. Runs in this layer are computationally intensive and resource demanding but will be executed infrequently and systematically using advanced Design of Experiments techniques. (2) A machine-learned surrogate emulation layer to train ultra-fast emulator models from simulation results and detect out-of-sample queries. While the government plans to develop and calibrate these surrogate emulators and analytical models in-house, the commercial solution must provide the extensible data staging, pipeline integration, and execution framework to ingest batch simulation results and host these government-developed models. (3) An intuitive self-service quantitative analysis layer housing pre-built methods for sensitivity analysis, marginal gain estimates, etc., and tools for custom analysis (e.g., tradespace decisions between range, speed, and lethality of weapon systems) and visualization. The solution must support both current operational needs and have flexibility to accommodate future growth in data volume, model complexity, user demand, and computational intensity. This next generation environment will establish an open, scalable, and unified computational backbone designed to modernize Department decision support. The scope of this effort includes the following core technical and performance requirements. A high-performance compute environment sized to meet demanding modeling, simulation, and analytic workloads. Proposed solution architectures should span options to allow for parameter evaluation in the simulation layer on the order of 1,200 individual simulations (i.e., light case - isolated missions only) to be executed within 10 hours real-time, up to 150,000 individual simulations (i.e., heavy case � full joint campaign) to be executed within 2 weeks real-time. Of note, current CAPE architecture would require 1 year of simulation execution runtime for the heavy case. Secure, efficient, data and software movement both into and out of the environment, as well as the ability to interface with external networks to enable transfer of data in accordance with applicable security and access controls. The environment must support network throughput of 100 Mbps - 1 Gbps. The solution must also support connectivity over HTTPS to designated external OSW and mission-relevant data sources, including OSW CAPE-furnished databases and other authorized repositories (e.g., War Data Platform), as applicable. Ability to accommodate evolving development ecosystems and diverse sets of software including M&S tools and analytic technologies. This includes modern software (e.g., Python, R, Java, etc.), scalable data platforms, scalable parallelizable processes (e.g., containers), optimization tools (e.g., GAMS), artificial intelligence capabilities (e.g., large language models), and neural network development (e.g., PyTorch), provided they can be incorporated in a secure and maintainable manner. The solution must enable efficient onboarding, integration, and removal of models and software as mission needs evolve. The Government will retain full operational tenant administration, maintaining exclusive control over user access provisioning, role-based security permissions, data ingestion, proprietary model uploads, container orchestration, and analytical query execution. The Commercial provider will be responsible for turnkey, managed platform and infrastructure IT operations, including hardware availability, operating system patching, network performance, automated system backups, and baseline cybersecurity hardening, ensuring government analysts and technical leads are fully insulated from day-to-day hardware maintenance and IT administration.

title: 6810--Bulk Road Salt for VA Medical Center Central Western MA
description: AMENDMENT NO. 2 SOLICITATION NO. 36C24127Q0028 DATE: 11/6/2026 1. THE SOLICITATION IS HEREBY AMENDED AS FOLLOWS: The following Questions and Answers, submitted by prospective offerors by October 30, 2026, at 4 PM EST, are incorporated into this solicitation. The Government s responses modify and/or clarify the solicitation. Revision to CLIN 0001 delivery requirement: Delete: "Initial delivery of Bulk Road Salt, 98% sodium chloride road salt and calcium chloride with CMA ice melt, delivered in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Delivery required prior to November 15, 2026 and replace with "Initial delivery of Bulk Road Salt, delivered in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The initial 40-ton delivery shall be completed no later than November 23, 2026." d. Revision to Performance Work Statement: Under Item Description and Salient Characteristics, revise the following sentence: Delete: "Initial delivery to take place prior to November 15, 2026, then as requested between November 15 until April 30th, 2027" and replace with Initial delivery of 40 tons shall be completed no later than November 23, 2026. Subsequent deliveries shall be provided as requested by the Government between November 15, 2026, and April 30, 2027." e. Revision to quoter submissions: Delete (4) Certifications in accordance with section 7.1. f. Offerors shall acknowledge receipt of amendments with their quotation submission. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. Vendors are reminded to review all other aspects of the solicitation and consider this amendment when preparing their responses. 2. RFI QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS: RFI s for Bulk Road Salt at VA Central Western MA Note: This version consolidates overlapping and duplicate vendor questions Product requirements 1. Please clarify whether CLINs 0001 and 0002 require (a) plain bulk sodium chloride road salt, (b) one pre-treated blend containing sodium chloride, calcium chloride, and CMA, or (c) separate road-salt and ice-melt products. Please confirm that CMA means calcium magnesium acetate and, if a blend is required, provide the required concentrations or an acceptable reference product. Also confirm whether magnesium may be substituted for calcium while maintaining the required overall composition. a. We do not require plain bulk sodium chloride. B. Yes, we require a blend that is premixed. C. No separate products. CMA is calcium magnesium acetate. We are seeking a blend of 85/15 Blend (85% Sodium Chloride + 15% Calcium Chloride Pellets by Weight. Magnesium can be substituted. 2. Is 98% sodium chloride a minimum acceptance requirement for every delivery measured on a dry-weight basis, or a nominal specification? Please identify applicable standards, including grade, grain size, testing or certificate-of-analysis requirements, and clarify which product is subject to the 4% maximum moisture limit. Would material with a typical sodium chloride content of 95-96% be unacceptable? We would prefer to adhere to ASTMD 632 which states not less than 95% blend specification. The 4% applies to calcium chloride and CMA products. 3. If road salt and calcium chloride/CMA ice melt are separate products, what quantity of each is required, should they be priced as separate sub-line items, and must the ice melt be delivered in bulk or bags? If bagged or palletized material is acceptable, specify the required bag size and whether the contractor must empty the bags into the salt shed and remove packaging. No separate products are required. Bagged or palletized material will not be considered. Quantities and ordering 4. Please confirm the total estimated quantity, the initial required quantity, and the deadline for the initial delivery. description: The requirement is for providing Gardening Services for properties owned or managed by the United States Government as official office and operational space for the Mission in Bogot�, Colombia. The Contractor shall provide comprehensive gardening and landscape maintenance services for the U.S. Embassy Bogota compound. These services shall include all planning, administration, and management necessary to ensure compliance with the contract, the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) schedules and instructions, and all applicable best practices, laws, and regulations. The Contractor must meet all performance standards specified in the contract. The Contractor shall also perform all related support functions, including but not limited to human resources management, quality control, technical oversight, and phytosanitary supervision. The green areas of the U.S. Embassy Bogota compound cover approximately 28,000 square meters, as highlighted in the reference image below. Areas requiring gardening services include lawns, trees, palms, shrubs, hedges, bushes, vines, ground cover, flower beds, and selected indoor plants. In addition, the scope of services includes all roofs and hard surfaces where activities must be performed, as described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The scope also includes the immediate exterior perimeter, primarily planters and exterior gardens at the entrances to the Embassy compound. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, and a possibility of 6 months extension if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The Contractor shall verify these conditions during the site walkthrough as part of the Request for Proposal (RFP) process The Government may award the contract based on the initial offer without discussion. The resultant contract will be a firm fixed price type contract. title: 6550--Sources Sought: Tuberculosis Testing Reagents and Consumables for the Buffalo VA Medical Center. In support of the Tuberculosis (TB) Testing Program
description: THIS REQUEST IS FOR SOURCES SOUGHT AND IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. THE SUBMISSION OF PRICING, CAPABILITIES FOR PLANNING PURPOSES, AND OTHER MARKET INFORMATION IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) RFO FAR 15.101(c). DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this Sources Sought Notice is marked as proprietary and will be handled accordingly. IAW RFO FAR 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought Notice. SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS code 334516 analytical laboratory instrument manufacturing (size standard of 1,000 employees). Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice, a solicitation announcement may be published. Responses to this sources sought synopsis are not considered adequate responses for a solicitation announcement. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VISN 02 Network Contracting Office, in support of the Buffalo VA Medical Center, is seeking sources capable of furnishing testing reagents and associated consumables necessary to perform tuberculosis testing for VISN 2 that at a minimum meets the following salient characteristics listed below. The contractor shall provide all reagents, controls, consumables, and related materials required for the successful performance of tuberculosis testing. Items may include, but are not limited to: Tuberculosis test kits. Positive and negative controls. Cell separation and processing reagents. Required consumables and ancillary supplies. Manufacturer-provided quality control materials. Product inserts and technical documentation. Technical support services. The VA is seeking a domestic source (manufactured in the United States) equivalent to the following salient characteristics: The required reagents shall: Be compatible with the T-SPOT® TB testing platform and methodology. Be FDA-cleared for clinical diagnostic use in the United States, as applicable. Be new, unused, and commercially available. Be delivered in original manufacturer packaging. Include sufficient remaining shelf life upon delivery. Meet all manufacturer specifications for testing accuracy and performance. Be suitable for use in a clinical laboratory environment accredited under applicable standards. Include all documentation necessary for use, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance. Be supported by manufacturer technical assistance and customer support. Be capable of maintaining continuity of supply throughout the contract period. The information identified above is intended to be descriptive, not restrictive and to indicate the quality of the supplies/services that will be satisfactory. It is the responsibility of the interested source to demonstrate to the government that the interested parties can provide the supplies/services that fulfill the required specifications. If you are interested and are capable of providing the sought out supplies/services, please provide the requested information as well as the information indicated below. Response to this notice should include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the following questions: Please indicate the size status and representations of your business, such as but not limited to: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Hubzone, Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), Large Business, etc.)? Is your company considered small under the NAICS code identified under this RFI? Are you the manufacturer, distributor, or an equivalent solution to the items being referenced above? If you are a large business, do you have any designated distributors? If so, please provide their company name, telephone, point of Contact and size status (if available). title: Reverse Industry Day and Listening Session � Emerging Acquisition Strategies for Future Projects
description: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Charleston District (SAC) Subject: Reverse Industry Day and Listening Session � Emerging Acquisition Strategies for Future Projects The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Charleston District (SAC), invites industry partners to participate in a Reverse Industry Day focused on emerging acquisition strategies and project delivery methods. This event is intended to foster open dialogue between industry and USACE regarding innovative approaches to design and construction procurement. BACKGROUND Industry partners have gained significant experience implementing progressive and collaborative delivery methods, including Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DB2B), Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC), and Other Transaction Authorities (OTA). USACE is exploring opportunities to expand the use of these tools where appropriate and seeks direct feedback from industry to help shape future acquisition strategies and solicitation approaches. Rather than conducting individual capability briefings, USACE will convene industry representatives in a roundtable forum to share lessons learned, discuss best practices, and identify opportunities to improve project delivery outcomes. EVENT OBJECTIVE This Reverse Industry Day is designed to provide industry with a platform to: � Share real-world experiences and lessons learned using emerging acquisition methods. � Discuss successful implementation strategies, challenges, and risk mitigation approaches. � Provide recommendations on solicitation structure, evaluation criteria, partnering practices, and contract administration considerations. � Offer feedback that may inform future USACE acquisition planning and solicitation development. TOPICS OF INTEREST Discussion topics may include, but are not limited to: � Other Transaction Authorities (OTA) � Progressive Design-Build (PDB) � Design-Build to Budget (DB2B) � Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC) � Early contractor involvement � Collaborative project development � Cost and schedule certainty � Innovation and risk-sharing approaches � Best practices for owner-contractor collaboration EVENT INFORMATION Date: Thursday, November 19, 2026 Time: 1:00 PM � 3:30 PM (EST) Location: Charleston District Headquarters 69A Hagood Ave Charleston, SC 29403 FORMAT Industry-to-USACE Roundtable Discussion Presenter Option: The Government, at its sole discretion, may select up to five (5) industry partners to present a case study (see form link, to be provided below). Selected presenters will be allotted: � 15-minute presentation � 15-minute question-and-answer session Case studies should focus on practical application of one or more of the acquisition strategies identified above and highlight lessons learned that may benefit future USACE procurements. A suggested case study format is attached for your consideration. REGISTRATION Please note: registration will remain open until Thursday, November 12, 2026, or until event capacity is reached. Registration information will be provided at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/fqAnY3zkjX ATTENDANCE LIMITATIONS � Attendance is limited to one (1) to two (2) representatives per company. � Maximum attendance is four companies/organizations due to time and capacity. � Participation will be in-person only. WHO SHOULD ATTEND Industry partners with demonstrated experience in: � Progressive Design-Build � Design-Build to Budget � Integrated Design and Construction � Other Transaction Authorities � Alternative and innovative project delivery methods Expected USACE participation includes representatives from Charleston District (SAC), South Atlantic Division (SAD), and other USACE members involved in project delivery, engineering, construction, contracting, and program management. DISCLAIMER This announcement is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government. Participation in this event is voluntary and at no cost to the Government. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with participation. Information exchanged during this event may be used by USACE to inform future acquisition strategies, project delivery approaches, and solicitation development; however, no procurement decisions will be made as a result of this event.

title: OK FW TSM 10(1) NFH Entrance Road and Parking Improvements
description: PROJECT NUMBER: OK FW TSM 10(1) PROJECT NAME: NFH Entrance Road and Parking Improvements PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Tishomingo National Fish Hatchery (NFH) is in south-central Oklahoma off SH 7 on a 220-acre U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) facility approximately 8 miles northwest of the Town of Tishomingo. The project will address deteriorated pavement for the entrance loop, adding a small parking area at the northeast corner of the entrance loop, and pavement of the entrance road and parking area south of HWY 7. The 3R project will provide new driving surface, entrance gates, culverts, Architectural Barriers Act (ABA) compliant parking spot, and ABA compliant curb ramp. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project will consist of full depth reclamation of the existing roads asphalt to a depth of 6-in, paving 3-in of asphalt, super elevation correction, and culvert replacement. New parking areas will be constructed with new aggregate base and asphalt pavement. A concrete ABA compliant curb ramp and ABA compliant parking spot. Concrete aprons will be placed around existing structures to match existing. Two new gates at the entrances to the NFH will also be installed. Entrance roads and parking areas will be closed during construction. description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH.? 1.3 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES Interested firms should submit information as to the capabilities, capacity, and experience to provide an MWS as set forth below: The MWS must alert the F-15EX aircrew to the presence of missiles that may threaten the aircraft without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six (6) pre-existing F-15EX sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. It must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel without requiring any change to aircraft configuration beyond installation of MWS line replaceable units (LRUs) in the six (6) pre-existing locations in the aircraft dedicated for missile warning. To avoid compromise of classified information, this notice does not ask for threat missile launch and approach detection performance for various use cases nor for an MWS concept of operations. AFLCMC/WAQ may contact you to ask for detection performance information if your response to this Sources Sought notice indicates your MWS is integrable in an F-15EX aircraft. Questions: What is the name of the MWS you describe in your response to this Sources Sought notice? Please include titles, abbreviations, and nomenclature as available. Please only identify and describe a single MWS in your response. On what Department of War (DoW) aircraft model(s) is your MWS approved for operational use today? Approval for operational use requires both 1) determination of airworthiness of the aircraft with your MWS integrated and 2) sustainment of the aircraft�s cybersecurity Authorization to Operate. Does your MWS consist only of sensor LRUs or does your MWS consist of sensor LRUs connected to a central processing LRU? If MWS sensors are connected to a central processor, how are they connected? What are the dimensions of each LRU in your MWS? You are alternately welcome to include in your response figures from engineering drawings that identify dimensions, rather than listing dimensions. How much does each LRU in your MWS weigh? How are your MWS�s LRUs physically fastened to an aircraft? What are your MWS�s electrical power requirements? Through what cable connection(s) is your MWS powered by the aircraft? What are your MWS�s cooling requirements? Through what interface(s) is your MWS cooled by the aircraft? Can your MWS be connected to an aircraft�s MIL-STD-1553 avionics bus? title: Hill AFB Hazardous Waste Removal and Disposal
description: THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, including 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small businesses that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work requires the transportation and disposal of Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) Hazardous wastes, non-RCRA wastes, Batteries, Corrosive waste, Compressed Gas Cylinders, Flammable waste, Demil-required waste, State-Regulated waste, Non-Hazardous Waste, Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), AFFF and other Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)-related waste, Mandatory Recycling waste, Reactive waste, and Toxic waste in and around Hill AFB, Utah. In addition, special services will be required such as sampling and analysis, industrial cleaning services, lab packs/loose packs, rolloff box rentals, vacuum box rentals, FRAC Tank rentals, and expedited removals and performance. All services necessary for the collection, storage, processing, removal, transportation, final treatment, and disposal of waste must be in accordance with all local, state, Department of Defense, and Federal laws and regulations. In a set aside, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008) states the small business Offeror/Contractor agrees to not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Note: The FAR references in the clause above are not aligned with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (see DEVIATION 2026-O0038); therefore, the following is provided for clarification purposes: references to 19.8 is now 19.105, 9.13 is now 19.106, 19.14 is now 19.107, 19.15 is now 19.108, 8.405-5 is now 8.4, and 16.505(b)(2)(i)(F) is now 16.5. In accordance with 13 CFR � 125.6(h), contractors may be subject to a minimum $500,000 fine if awarded a contract with this clause and does not meet the requirement. DLA has identified the majority of RCRA TSDFs (Treatment, Storage, Disposal Facilities) in the industry as large businesses. All TSDFs used during the performance of this contract must be approved and listed on the Qualified Facilities List located at the following website: https://www.dla.mil/DispositionServices/Offers/Disposal/HazardousWaste/HazWasteDisposal/. Given there is a lack of small business ownership of TSDFs and that disposal costs make up a large portion of the contract dollar value, there is a reasonable probability that a small business would pay more than 50% of the cost of the contract to large businesses. *The Government intends to solicit proposals on SAM.gov and award a commercial Firm-Fixed Priced, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Services Contract. The contract is anticipated to have one 30-month base period, followed by one 30-month option period. There is no solicitation available at this time. However, attached is a DRAFT Price Schedule and DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS) that entities responding to this Sources Sought should use to help determine if they would be able to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting requirements. IF YOUR ENTITY IS CAPABLE OF PERFORMING THE REQUESTED SERVICES, WITHOUT THE LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, THE CAPABILITIES PACKAGE DETAILED BELOW IS NOT REQUIRED. In accordance with FAR 6.101(a) (DEVIATION 2026-O0017 Revision 2), with certain limited exceptions, contracting officers must obtain full and open competition by using competitive procedures to solicit offers and award Government contracts. If your entity would like to respond to this Sources Sought, but is unable to meet the limitations on subcontracting, please email lacie.kaiser@dla.mil with �SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ] HILL� in the subject line, stating your entity�s Notification of Interest (a capabilities package is not required). SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested entities must demonstrate their ability to perform the requested services, described above, by submitting a brief capabilities package (no more than three pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum). This documentation must identify, at a minimum: (1) Company name, office location(s), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and a statement identifying small business category(ies) and current status of the small business classification; (2) Relevant experience within the last five years, including any contract number(s), names of individuals responsible for the referenced contracts/projects, and current telephone numbers for those individuals; if you were a subcontractor, identify the work you actually performed as the sub-contractor; and (3) If a small business, a statement identifying your entity�s ability to perform in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), as well as an explanation of how you would be able to comply with this requirement considering the disposal requirements within the draft price schedule that is anticipated to be included in the contract. (4) A listing of TSDFs your entity would use during the performance of this contract, identifying each TSDF as similarly situated or not as your entity. The submittal package must be emailed to lacie.kaiser@dla.mil with �SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ WASTE HILL� in the subject line. The submittal package must be received no later than 4:30pm Eastern Time, November 12, 2026. Any submission after the specified time and date will not be considered unless it is received before the review of other submissions has started and the Contracting Officer determines that accepting the late submission would not unduly delay the acquisition. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition is in the Government's best interest. If an unrestricted solicitation is issued, then the FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008) would not apply. All responsible entities, including small businesses, are eligible to submit a proposal in response to an unrestricted solicitation. A response to this Sources Sought will not be considered an adequate response to any forthcoming solicitation announcement. The Government WILL NOT provide a debriefing on the results of the survey. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought notice or any follow-up information requests. All information submitted will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purpose intended.

title: Main Rotor Spindle Pry Bars (P/N SPB-60-RS, NSN 3040-01 722-4706)
description: This Sources Sought notice is being posted to satisfy the requirements of Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.302-170. The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with EAA Tools, LLC (EEA), CAGE: 5LNR7, for the award of a contract. The designated contractor, EEA, shall provide to NAWCAD Lakehurst the manufacture and delivery of the Main Rotor Spindle Pry Bars (P/N SPB-60-RS, NSN 3040-01-722-4706) for the Royal Australian Navy (RAN); Danish Defense Acquisition and Logistics Organization (DALO); and the India Navy (IN) in support of the MH-60R program. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 332216 (Saw Blade and Handtool Manufacturing). The Product Service Code (PSC) is 3040 (Miscellaneous Power Transmission Equipment). THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible small and large businesses, capable of fulfilling the requirements described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this Notice. EAA Tools, LLC. is the OEM, sole designer, developer and manufacturer of the Main Rotor Spindle Pry Bar. The Main Rotor Spindle Pry Bar securely attaches to spindle damper mount and provides required leverage and stability to manipulate main rotor spindle assembly on aircraft for various maintenance requirements to include access to spindle mounts bolts and pitch control rod removal/re-installation. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements" for this action. (THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS.) Responsible, interested parties, however, may identify their interest by submitting a capabilities statement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not pay for any responses received. There is no commitment by the Government to issue any solicitations, make an award or awards, or be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties before award of a contract for the efforts mentioned above. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract. No telephone responses will be accepted.
