title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) Laboratory Testing
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) is seeking laboratories to validate the capabilities of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTDs). This initiative supports the Department of the Army�s goal of providing potable drinking water for Soldiers from any indigenous fresh water source, which enhances Soldier lethality by reducing load and increasing the duration of autonomous squad-level operations. The Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of PdM SCIE, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify laboratories with the required certifications, equipment, and personnel to conduct this validation testing. The information gathered from this RFI will inform a future request for proposal. The Government reserves the right to cancel this opportunity or make no awards in conjunction with this opportunity. This is a Request for Information ONLY and not a request for proposal. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The objective of this effort is to validate the ability of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTD) to perform clearance of microbiological contaminants and Toxic Industrial Chemicals/Toxic Industrial Materials (TIC/TIMs). Testing must be conducted according to the military-specific purification standards outlined in National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Protocols P248.01 and P248.02. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to, the following laboratory capabilities: Certification to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. Ability to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. Capability to draft product-specific test plans in accordance with the P248 validation scheme. Commitment to provide all raw data, test data, and internal standard data. SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is seeking information from qualified sources that can address the stated requirements. All responses to this announcement will be governed by the instructions herein. Interested parties are requested to submit information packages that present their planned approach to addressing the testing objectives. Packages should focus on the laboratory�s technical approach, capabilities, and relevant experience. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. All submissions must be submitted electronically via the email instructions included herein. c. Submissions sent through other channels or after the response period has ended will not be reviewed or evaluated. d. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs will be at the expense of the interested party. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties shall include the following information in their response: A statement confirming if the laboratory is certified to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. A statement confirming if the laboratory is equipped to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. If subletting work to another laboratory, provide name, credentials and last audit of that laboratory An estimated timeline for executing the validation testing, assuming an award in Nov/Dec 2026. Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Supporting technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, illustrations). Company background, business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses shall be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Responses received after this time and date may not be considered. The subject line for responses shall read: �Response to IWTD Laboratory Testing RFI, [Vendor�s Business Name]� SECTION 5 - Government Points of Contact Any questions for clarification regarding this opportunity may be emailed to the POCs listed below no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain proprietary or classified information. Primary Points of Contact Primary Point of Contact Eric Brack eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Phone: 508-206-3968 Secondary Point of Contact Blaise Liess blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Phone: 703-223-1993

description: MILITARY SEALIFT COMMAND (MSC) Sources Sought N102D-SS27-SHRED 27 October 2026 Subject: SHRED SERVICES IN NORFOLK VIRGINIA DESCRIPTION: This is a market survey for acquisition planning purposes, and no formal solicitation exists at this time. MSC is soliciting input to determine the technical, administrative, management and financial capability of potential offerors to perform this kind of work. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, materials, supervision, and transportation necessary to perform on-site collection and destruction services for MSC facilities located On Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia. Other locations in the Hampton Roads, Virginia area may be added upon contract modification. All shredding shall be to NSA standards. The Military Sealift Command (MSC) requires the secure and recurring destruction of non-record, classified/unclassified material marked up to and including SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL, and CUI / FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO). Classified and other sensitive materials include paper documents, digital media (e.g., CDs and DVDs), hard drives, and cell phones. This requirement does not include Top Secret material. The objective is to ensure all materials are destroyed in a manner that renders them completely unrecoverable in accordance with applicable security requirements. The Contractor shall service all designated collection points listed in the PWS. All Small Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, Certified Woman Owned Small Business Certified HUBZone and Certified 8(a) Small Businesses are encouraged to respond. The NAICS Code is 561990: All Other Support Services, and the Size Standard is $16.5M. There are two potential requirements that could be informed by this sources sought notice. One potential anticipated period of performance is a seven month period, with a total period of performance from 11 February 2027 � 12 August 2027. An additional potential period of performance is a one-year base period, plus four (4), one-year option periods with a total period of performance from 15 August 2027 � 14 August 2032. This information will be used by the Contracting Officer to assist in developing the procurement strategy, including whether a small business set-aside can be established, if the requirement should be sole sourced to large business, or whether small businesses and large businesses should be able to compete for work. If a small business set-aside is established, then FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, applies. Note that if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small businesses, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a small business set-aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14. This is a market research tool used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential business sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of an award. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this notice. Respondents will not be notified of the results, and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this notice. title: Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT)
description: SYNOPSIS: #N68335-26-Q-1204 Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division - F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Hydraulics International, Inc. (CAGE: 56529) for the Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) in support of the NAWCAD F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program. This order will procure one (1) APCLT (Part Number (P/N): 4129AS0100-1, National Stock Number (NSN): 4920-01-658-2036). The APCLT is required to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester will provide the means to meet the requirement and is required by the RAAF. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester is a portable unit that runs on facility supplied compressed air and that can supply various combinations of air flow and air pressure to check leakage and pressure regulation in aircraft cabins and canopy seals. Hydraulics International, Inc., as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the APCLT, is the only source with the requisite knowledge, technical experience, and production-level data to produce these components. The components being procured are integral to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure and are critical to maintaining operational readiness. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) is mandatory for consideration. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based on the responses to this notice will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for an award of a contract. description: The Defense Logistics Agency-Aberdeen, on behalf of the Army Integrated Logistics Supply Center (ILSC) � Supply Chain Management Directorate (SCMD) � Strategic Sourcing Directorate (SSD), intends to acquire Parts to support the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. Requirements Description: The load bank is a piece of electrical test equipment used to simulate an electrical load, to test an electric power source. The load bank is used to provide field preventive maintenance checks and services of the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The EPP III is the main electric power source for the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The load bank is used on the 150 KW, 400Hz generator sets on the EPP III. In the EPP III, this relay monitors electrical frequency and helps control or protect generator operations by opening or closing electrical circuits when frequency conditions change. Its function is critical to maintaining proper power quality and protecting connected equipment from abnormal operating conditions. The Government does not possess the technical data package (TDP) for the parts. The LOAD BANK, ELECTRICA was last purchased on 8/17/2026 through Contract # SPRBL1-20-D-0015 for a quantity of 21. At a minimum the support information you submit should include, but is not limited to, the following types of documentation: Questionnaire, drawings, test results, information on previous Government and commercial contracts, data rights, etc. In your response, please include your company name, CAGE code, and a technical point of contract with email address and telephone number. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this SSA or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this SSA. title: NATO Business Opportunity: Antenna Replacement at Atalanti SATCOM Ground Station
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for one new SATCOM Anchor Station antenna and associated Radome to be installed at Atalanti SATCOM Ground Station in Greece. To bid on this contract, potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 3) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 4) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement The reference for the solicitation is IFB-CO-424392-ARA and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Antenna System shall form part of the SATCOM anchoring component and shall support X-band SATCOM operations. The requirement covers the provision of supplies, installation, integration, and commissioning of a complete SATCOM RF head solution. The solution shall include an antenna with a diameter of at least 11 m, Radome, tracking, transmitting, and receiving subsystems, and all associate civil works and services. The RF-head will be integrated into the Atalanti/Greece SATCOM Anchoring Component and shall include the required electrical, data, IF and monitoring interfaces necessary for full system operation and integration within the existing site infrastructure. Objective: The expected result is a fully installed, integrated, tested, documented and accepted Antenna and Radome installation that: a. Meets the Antenna SRS, Radome and Civil Work SRS; b. Supports X-band SATCOM transmit and receive operation; c. Provides automatic satellite tracking capability; d. Provides environmental protection through a rigid, non-inflatable Radome; e. Provides compliant civil, electrical, grounding, bonding and lightning protection installation; f. Provides verified M&C integration with the site�s monitoring and control environment g. Provides tested safety interlocks, emergency stops, access controls and maintenance provisions; h. Provides complete documentation, including as-built drawings, training, and transition-to-operations support. Key Deliverables: Key deliverables include the RF-head and its associated antenna, tracking, Tx and Rx sub-systems; non-inflatable Radome; required civil and electrical works; IF and M&C cabling; installation and integration activities; service laptop; and complete as-built documentation. The contractor shall also provide all necessary cables, waveguides, connectors, interfaces and installation materials required for a complete operational solution. Final deliverables shall include the relevant interface documentation and as-built drawings covering the installed system and associated infrastructure. The complete solution shall be delivered fully installed, integrated with the existing system, tested, commissioned, and ready for operational use. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. U.S. firms can download a copy of the NCP application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. IMPORTANT DATES: Request a DOE (and, for firms new to NCP, submit the one-time NCP application): 12 November 2026 NCIA distributes the solicitation (planned): 16 November 2026 Bid closing (anticipated): 18 January 2027 Contract Award (estimated): 15 February 2027

description: Notice on Intent to Award a Sole Source Firm Fixed Price Contract The U.S. Department of the Treasury, Departmental Offices & Enterprise Procurement Branch, Treasury Common Services Center - Acquisition Services, intends to award a sole source contract to NK CONSULTING, INC. for a subscription to a commercial-off-the-shelf database that provides the Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence. The subscription shall provide authorized Government users with access to current and historical North Korea-focused information, including news reporting, expert analysis, official North Korean source materials, searchable research databases, and reference resources. The platform shall support the identification, monitoring, and analysis of political, economic, security, sanctions, trade, and other developments involving North Korea. At a minimum, the web-based subscription service shall provide the following capabilities: Access to North Korea-focused news, analysis, and research content; Searchable archives of historical articles, reports, and reference materials; Access to official North Korean government and state media publications and other primary-source content; Advanced search capabilities across all subscription content; Real-time updates, email notifications, and customizable alerts for significant developments; Integrated research and analytical resources related to North Korean leadership, sanctions, trade, maritime activity, aviation, missile activity, economic indicators, and other relevant subject areas; Regular newsletters, executive briefings, and periodic analytical publications; Access to historical and current data through a single, integrated subscription platform The Government has determined that NK CONSULTING Inc. is the only source capable of meeting the Government's requirements because NK CONSULTING Inc. developed a comprehensive North Korea-focused subscription. The aniticipated award is for a base period of 12-months, with four (4) option period(s), if applicable, from January 3, 2027 through January 2, 2031. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) for Reduction/Removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Materials
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) and the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center is conducting a market investigation to identify products and technologies for individual Soldier water purification. This effort focuses on capabilities for the reduction or removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals (TICs) and Toxic Industrial Materials (TIMs) from any indigenous fresh water sources. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks to identify suppliers of water treatment technologies that meet Buy American Act requirements and can be integrated with current and future equipment, such as the Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) and MOLLE Hydration System. Information gathered will be used for planning purposes to address military water purification needs. Respondents are encouraged to submit alternative technical approaches or product solutions that vary from the listed specifications, as long as they meet or exceed the core capability requirement. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for information and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not constitute a commitment by the U.S. Government. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The DEVCOM Soldier Center is interested in products and technologies that meet or have the potential to meet the following key performance parameters for individual water purification. Respondents should provide actual, demonstrated product performance for each parameter, including where performance does not meet specifications listed below: Contaminant Removal: Capable of removing TICs and TIMs to levels mandated by the Defense Health Agency (DCPH-A), as detailed in the attached "Toxic Industrial Chemical/Material Military Exposure Guideline." Compatibility: Compatible with standard military canteens and hydration systems. Physical Specifications: Weight: Not to exceed 12 oz. Size: Low bulk and compact. Operational Life: At least 135 liters. Shelf Life: 5-year storage stability with an 18-month unused service life. Environmental Resilience: System will not degrade in temperatures from -33�C to 52�C. Capable of treating water ranging in temperature from above freezing to 52�C (liquid water up to 52�C). Must not be impacted by freezing and remain functional upon thawing. Fully functional in all operational environments. Performance: Treat-to-Drink Time: Ideally less than 5 minutes (target less than 20 minutes). Flow Rate: Not less than 200 mL/min (if applicable). Water Quality: Processed water must be palatable, similar to commercial bottled water. Ease of use with or without gloved hands. Power: Batteries, if used, must be a commercially available type. Microbiological Mitigation: Ideally meets or exceeds requirements of NSF Protocol P248.01 (optional). SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is issued to identify interested sources and gather information on market capabilities. Participation is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding. Failure to respond does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. Submissions must be sent electronically via email as instructed below. c. The Government will not pay for any information, administrative costs, or product samples submitted in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties are invited to submit responses detailing their products, technologies, and capabilities. The submission should include: A description of current commercial product(s) and how they can address the military requirements. Technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, patents, illustrations). Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Product cost information. Company information: business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. A physical sample (optional; no payment will be made for unsolicited samples). Any relevant data on microbiological or chemical reductions. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses must be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Responses received after this time may not be considered. The subject line shall read: �Response to IWTD TIC/TIM RFI, [Vendor�s Business Name]� SECTION 5 - Government Points of Contact Any questions for clarification may be emailed to the POCs listed below no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Primary Point of Contact Eric Brack eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Phone: 508-206-3968 Secondary Point of Contact Blaise Liess blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Phone: 703-223-1993

title: Denmark – Industrial machinery – Delivery and installation of a ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for oxides and nitrides of silicon to become its new primary instrument for 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q3 2027. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. As an open access tool, the Instrument must support the full spectrum of etching of silicon-based dielectrics, from sub 100 nm nanostructures defined by electron beam lithography to depths of several tens of microns. Meeting these demands requires exceptional process controllability and tunability: the system must perform ultra precise, low-rate etches (< 100 nm/min) with smooth and straight sidewalls and minimal undercut for shallow features, alongside high etch rate deep etches (approaching 500 nm/min). It must also accommodate all silicon dielectrics of the form SixNy, SixOx and SixOyNz, and be compatible with mask materials including Si, Cr, e-beam resists and UV/DUV photoresists with high mask selectivity for all these masking materials. The user interface must be intuitive and user friendly. The Instrument should be engineered to the highest industrial standards to minimize maintenance, and any required servicing must be straightforward and efficient. The instrument must be configured for 150 mm wafer processing and a complete kit enabling the processing of 200 mm wafers must be included in the tender as an option. Furthermore, DTU will have the option to purchase one more ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics identical to the initial instrument.

description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die externe fachliche Unterstützung bei der Erstellung kommunaler Klimaanpassungskonzepte für kreisangehörige Kommune im Konvoi gemäß §29f KlimaG BW. Die Leistungen werden im Rahmen eines Rahmenvertrags erbracht und jeweils über Einzelabrufe für mehrere Kommunen eines Konvois beauftragt. Die Ausschreibung umfasst vier Konvois. Ein Konvoi umfasst mindestens drei bis maximal sieben kreisangehörige Kommunen. Die kommunenscharfen Konzepte für die Kommunen eines Konvois sollen jeweils innerhalb von 12 Monaten erstellt werden. Es finden maximal zwei Konvois zeitgleich statt. Sollte in einem Jahr kein Kommunen-Konvoi zustande kommen, kann der Auftraggeber Bedarfspositionen im Umfang von 40-85 Arbeitstagen beauf-tragen. Diese dienen der Wahrnehmung der Aufgaben des Landkreises nach KlimaG BW § 29f Absatz 1 Satz 3 „Unterstützung der kreisangehöri-gen Gemeinden bei der Anpassung an die Folgen des Klimawandels“. Sie stehen in unmittelbarem sachlichem Zusammenhang mit dem Auftragsge-genstand. Art und Zielsetzung dieser Bedarfspositionen werden im Einzel-abruf festgelegt. Die Vergütung erfolgt auf Grundlage der im Preisblatt ver-einbarten Positionen.

buyer: European Commission, DG EMPL - Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion
title: Luxembourg – Evaluation consultancy services – Study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and support to the preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework
description: This call for tenders is for an external independent study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and to support the contracting authority in relation to the open public consultation in preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework. The strategic framework sets out three crosscutting key objectives and a range of actions for promoting workers’ health and safety. The three objectives are: anticipating and managing change in the new world of work brought about by the green, digital and demographic transitions; improving prevention of workplace accidents and illnesses; increasing preparedness for any potential future health crises. The implementation of these three objectives is underpinned by: (i) social dialogue; (ii) strengthening of the evidence base; (iii) strengthening of enforcement; (iv) awareness raising; and (v) funding. At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. The results of this screening exercise study will inform the process of developing new EU OSH priorities in the strategic framework on health and safety at work after 2027.

description: The study should pursue two complementary objectives. First, it should estimate the elasticity of retail investment to tax incentives by analysing in order to determine how strongly tax advantages affect the likelihood to invest and the amounts invested. Second, it should assess the potential budgetary implications of introducing an SIA under different design scenarios, taking into account varying forms of tax incentives participation rates and substitution effects with existing savings products. This second objectives should be possibly combined with an assessment of second round effect of greater retail participation to capital markets on consumption and investment.. title: Germany – Agricultural services – Beratung landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe zur Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Biodiversität und Nachhaltigkeit in der Landwirtschaft (EB)
description: Für das ML soll eine Rahmenvereinbarung zur Erbringung von Beratungsdienstleistungen nach Art. 78 der EU Strategieplan VO (EU) 2021/2115 vom 2. Dezember 2021 vergeben werden. Ausgeschrieben werden definierte Beratungsdienstleistungen für landwirtschaftliche Betriebe. Die Maßnahme zielt auf die Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Nachhaltigkeit landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe unter besonderer Beachtung der Aspekte der Biodiversität, der Klimaresilienz, des Tierwohls und eines effizienten Umgangs mit Ressourcen durch Wissenstransfer. Die Beratungsleistungen sind nur dann förderfähig, wenn die Beratungen durch nach diesem Vergabeverfahren ausgewählte Beratungsanbieter und Beratungskräfte durchgeführt werden. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung - Fachlicher Teil (Teil B) und der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C) - sowie den weiteren beigefügten Anlagen zu entnehmen. Die Rahmenvereinbarung soll mit mehreren Unternehmen (§ 21 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 VgV) abgeschlossen werden, um den Landwirten eine Wahl des Beratungsanbieters zu ermöglichen. Dabei werden so viele Zuschläge entsprechend der Platzierung nach der Angebotswertung erteilt, bis die Angebotssummen der bezuschlagten Angebote die zur Verfügung stehende Fördersumme von 5.849.200 EUR im Vertragszeitraum 01. März 2027 - 30. Juni 2029 erreicht ist. Das zuletzt bezuschlagte Angebot wird daher voraussichtlich nicht in vollem Umfang berücksichtigt werden können, sondern nur insoweit bis die zur Verfügung stehenden Fördermittel ausgeschöpft sind. Das maximal mögliche Mittelvolumen je Beratungsanbieter in dem gesamten Vertragszeitraum wird im Rahmen des Vergabeverfahrens ermittelt, wobei je Beratungsanbieter maximal ein Betrag in Höhe von bis zu 300.000 EUR zugeteilt wird. Dieser Betrag kann im Fall einer späteren Zuteilung von gestrichenen Mitteln (s.u.) überschritten werden. Für den Fall, dass ein Beratungsanbieter seinen Betrag nicht benötigt/abruft, werden ihm Mittel gestrichen. Die dann frei gewordenen Mittel können an die anderen Beratungsanbieter zugewiesen werden. Weitere Einzelheiten hierzu finden sich in der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C). Der Abschluss der Rahmenvereinbarung bildet zunächst keinen Anspruch auf die Mittel und stellt keine Erteilung einer Zuwendung dar. Hierfür muss im Rahmen des Zuwendungsverfahrens ein separater Förderantrag gestellt und dieser bewilligt werden (siehe hierzu auch Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C)).

title: Germany – Landscaping work – Stiftung Schloss Marienburg: Bauabschnitt 2: Garten- und Landschaftsbau: Oberbauschichten
description: Die Stiftung Schloss Marienburg beabsichtigt die Sanierung des Schlosses. Das Gebäude ist ein eingetragenes Baudenkmal. Die historische Bausubstanz ist zu schonen und zu erhalten. Die Erfordernisse aus dem Denkmalschutz verlangen von allen am Bau beteiligten Firmen eine besondere Vorsicht und Sorgfalt und eine enge Abstimmung mit der Bauleitung. Sanierung des Schlosses Marienburg, Bauabschnitte 2.1 Hangsicherung und 2.2 Terrasse Süd - Garten- und Landschaftsbauarbeiten zur Herstellung von Oberbauschichten, Pflasterbelägen und Entwässerungsanlagen. Die Leistungen umfassen insbesondere Erdarbeiten, Herstellung von Bodenaufbauten, Ziegelpflaster und wassergebundenen Wegedecken, Abdichtungs- und Dränagearbeiten, Entwässerungsleitungen und -rinnen sowie Entsorgung und Dokumentation. Der zu sanierende Hangbereich besteht aus einer bis zu rund 13 m hohen und bis zu rund 65° gegenüber der Horizontalen geneigten Festgesteinswand aus Buntsandstein. Im oberen Bereich des Hanges befindet sich ein historischer Laubengang, der mittels einer Gewölbekonstruktion auf dem Hang aufgelagert ist. Aufgrund von eindringendem Wasser und Bewuchs haben sich Teile der Felsoberfläche gelöst, wodurch die Auflagerpunkte der tragenden Konsolsteine teilweise nicht mehr vorhanden sind. Der Laubengang wird derzeit durch eine Stahlkonstruktion notabgestützt und ist gesperrt. Im Rahmen der Sanierung wird der Bodenaufbau des Laubengangs einschließlich Pflasterbelag, Abdichtung und Entwässerung erneuert. Im Bauabschnitt 2.2 ist die Nutzbarmachung der Terrasse Süd vorgesehen. Hierzu wird die vorhandene Betonoberfläche zurückgebaut und ein neuer Bodenaufbau mit wassergebundener Wegedecke hergestellt. Bestandteil der Maßnahmen ist außerdem die Erneuerung der Entwässerung sowie die Herstellung der erforderlichen Oberbauschichten auf den Stahlbetondecken. Die Arbeiten erfolgen unter besonderer Berücksichtigung des Denkmalschutzes und der historischen Bausubstanz.

description: Die Südwestfalen-IT (SIT), ein kommunaler IT-Dienstleister für derzeit 72 Kommunen und kommunale Einrichtungen in Nordrhein-Westfalen, beabsichtigt den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung über die Lieferung, Einführung, Pflege und Weiterentwicklung von Fachanwendungen der VOIS-Plattform sowie die Erbringung damit zusammenhängender Dienstleistungen. Ziel ist die weitere Standardisierung und Konsolidierung der kommunalen Verfahrenslandschaft sowie die Erweiterung einer bereits produktiv betriebenen, einheitlichen und integrierten VOIS-Plattform für Fachverfahren der öffentlichen Verwaltung. Die Lösungen müssen in die bestehende VOIS-Betriebsumgebung der SIT integriert werden und eine medienbruchfreie Zusammenarbeit mit vorhandenen Fachverfahren, Dokumentenmanagement-, Archiv-, Finanz- und Bürgerportalsystemen ermöglichen. Die Vergabe erfolgt in fünf Fachlosen: 1) Gewerbe- und Gewerbeaufsichtswesen, 2) Einwohnermelde- und Passwesen einschließlich Wahlen, 3) Bürgerbüro/Bürgerdienste, 4) Terminplanung und Terminorganisation, 5) Allgemeine Verwaltung, insbesondere Gebührenkasse, Statistik und digitale Archivierung. Die zu beschaffenden Lösungen müssen den einschlägigen fachlichen, technischen, datenschutzrechtlichen und informationssicherheitsbezogenen Anforderungen des öffentlichen Sektors entsprechen, insbesondere hinsichtlich OZG-Konformität, XÖV-Standards, DSGVO, Barrierefreiheit sowie aktueller Anforderungen an Informations- und Cybersicherheit. Die Rahmenvereinbarung soll den bedarfsgerechten Abruf von Leistungen für die SIT und die von ihr betreuten Kommunen ermöglichen und die langfristige Digitalisierung kommunaler Verwaltungsleistungen unterstützen.
